turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m Dr. AI. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, Dr. AI, it's nice to meet you. I guess what brings me in is... well, it’s this feeling I get. I’ve been working as a building cleaner for a long time—I actually have my associate's degree, but I like the cleaning work because I get to stay on my feet and keep busy, you know? But the real problem is whenever I’m actually supposed to just sit still. 

Like, we have these mandatory staff meetings at work where the supervisor just drones on about safety protocols or whatever, or even on the weekends when I help out at my parish and we have these church event briefings... I just, I feel like I’ve got this motor humming right under my skin. It’s like a physical buzz, almost. I try to just sit there and be respectful, but I end up shifting around in my chair, crossing and uncrossing my legs, and eventually I just have to stand up and pace in the back of the room. Or I’ll find some excuse to leave, like, "Oh, I better go check the supply closet," or "I need to grab some water," just so I can move around. It's like I just can't stay planted in a chair without feeling like I'm going to jump out of my own body, and it's starting to really bother people when I'm constantly up and down like that.

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient describes shifting around in their chair and crossing/uncrossing their legs when expected to sit still.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient reports standing up to pace or finding excuses to leave during mandatory meetings where they are expected to remain seated.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes an intense internal restlessness, feeling like they are going to jump out of their own body if they sit still.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient explicitly describes feeling like they have a 'motor humming right under my skin' and prefers jobs that keep them on their feet and busy.

turns.doctor_question: When you have that feeling of needing to move around, are you also feeling anxious or worried?
turns.patient_response:
Anxious? No, no, it's not really like that at all. I mean, people ask me that sometimes—my sister is always saying, "What are you so stressed about?" when she sees me tapping my foot or pacing around her living room, but I always have to tell her, I'm not stressed! I'm not worried about anything. I'm not sitting in those staff meetings thinking about, you know, whether I paid the electric bill or if my car needs new tires or if I'm doing a bad job at work. My mind isn't spinning with worries or anything like that. 

It's really just... it's entirely physical. Like my muscles themselves are just awake and ready to do something, and they don't care that my brain knows I'm supposed to be sitting and listening. I remember just last month, Father Thomas at the parish was giving this extremely long, detailed update on the roof repair fund—and I wasn't worried about the roof at all, I knew we had the money from the bake sale and the silent auction and everything—but I still had to get up and walk to the back of the fellowship hall. I just couldn't sit in that metal folding chair for another second. 

So, no, it's not a nervous thing or a fearful thing. I don't get panic attacks or sit there dreading things. It's just this... this raw energy that has absolutely nowhere to go if I'm just parked in a seat. I'm actually usually in a pretty good mood, I just want to be in a good mood while I'm moving, you know? If I'm sitting, I'm just thinking about how much I want to be walking, not about anything bad happening.

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient mentions that her sister often sees her tapping her foot.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient describes having to get up and walk to the back of the hall because she couldn't remain seated during a meeting.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes pacing around and feeling a physical restlessness and 'raw energy' when forced to sit.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes having 'raw energy' and muscles that are 'awake and ready to do something,' akin to being driven by a motor.
symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies feeling anxious, stressed, or having her mind spin with worries.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had accidents where stool leaked or you couldn’t make it to the bathroom in time?
turns.patient_response:
What? No, no, definitely not. I've never had anything like that happen. I mean, I know I just said I'm always looking for an excuse to get up and move around, and I did mention going to check the supply closet or getting water... and sure, sometimes I'll say I need to use the restroom just to get out of my chair for a few minutes. Like during those long safety meetings I told you about, I'll definitely take a bathroom break just to stretch my legs and walk down the hall. 

But it's never because of an emergency, you know? It's not because I can't hold it or because I'm having any sort of accident. My digestion and all that, it's completely fine. Regular as a clock. I've been very lucky with my health in that regard, honestly. My buddy Frank, he's got some issues with that kind of thing, always having to map out where the bathrooms are when we go anywhere, but for me? Never an issue. When I get up, it's purely just because my legs are practically screaming at me to move, not because of any bathroom emergencies. So, no, absolutely nothing like that.

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient admits to making excuses to leave their seat during long meetings just to get up and walk around.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes a strong internal sense of restlessness, stating their legs are 'practically screaming at me to move.'
